statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6478 (PostgreSQL discloses MD5-hashed passwords via covert timing channel) in 16.14 on the PostgreSQL 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6478/ lists 16.14 as the fixed release for major version 16 (versions before 16.14 are affected), and the 16.14 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.14/, list this CVE. The fix is commits https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/1604939b2210b93e34572ee6df499d103849c53e (adds timingsafe_bcmp(), a constant-time comparison) and https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/00e27235e5ef6596acc94ec60eb17f74810bf817 (uses it in the server's MD5 and SCRAM authentication code, src/backend/libpq/crypt.c, auth.c and auth-scram.c) on the REL_16_STABLE branch; both are tagged Security: CVE-2026-6478 and are in the REL_16_14 release tag and not in REL_16_13. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; the 16.14-r0 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/56de254843f841a99aedea4953a2dc9ec9338eb4/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, differs from the 16.13-r0 one only in the version and tarball checksum, applies no patch that touches the files this fix changes, and lists CVE-2026-6478 under its 16.14-r0 secfixes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres, in every postgresql16 build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI package repository as of 2026-11-27, on both x86_64 and aarch64 (package checksums verified against the package index): 16.13-r0 reports PostgreSQL 16.13 and is affected, while 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 report 16.14, 16.15 and 16.16 and carry the fix. As a check, the server binary references timingsafe_bcmp in 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 on both architectures and not in 16.13-r0. 16.14-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

CVE-2026-6478 (PostgreSQL discloses MD5-hashed passwords via covert timing channel) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 18.4: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6478/ lists 18.4 as the fixed release for major version 18. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/d93ef413174daae721c6f2cfda3fbd5187f0b4ee ('Apply timingsafe_bcmp() in authentication paths') on the REL_18_STABLE branch. Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-6478 under its 18.4-r0 secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with that APKBUILD from the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version. We checked every postgresql18 build published for Alpine 3.23 as of 2026-11-27 (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64. In each, the postgres server reports the PostgreSQL release matching the package version. The fix replaces seven password and nonce comparisons in the server (crypt.c, auth.c and auth-scram.c) with calls to timingsafe_bcmp, which the server already contained; counting call instructions to timingsafe_bcmp in a disassembly of /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres (postgresql18 package) gives 1 in 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0 and 18.3-r0 and 8 in 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0. 18.4-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 carrying the fix; 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0 and 18.3-r0 are affected.
